messages.author: c89471eda5dca12c
messages.subject: Residual Analysis
parts:
I am building a PA model using lavaan, I extracted some fit measures:SRMR, RMR, CFI, TLI RMSEA, so I would like also to evaluate the residuals to make my evaluation more strong.

So executing the code below given from Keith A. Markus: 

library(lavaan)

# The Holzinger and Swineford (1939) example
HS.model <- ' visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
speed   =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '

fit <- lavaan(HS.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939,
              auto.var=TRUE, auto.fix.first=TRUE,
              auto.cov.lv.x=TRUE)
summary(fit, fit.measures=TRUE)


# View Residuals (documentation in the lavaan-class help file)
resid(fit, type='raw')
resid(fit, type='cor')
resid(fit, type='normalized')
resid(fit, type='standardized')

I got the results:

So based on this results I can say my model above had not a good fit since the values in covariance matrix of residuals are high?

Except for x5 to x4 that is 0.070. 

In another case if all values are low like 0.004 for example with also good SRMR, RMR, CFI, TLI RMSEA I can say my model had a good fit over data?

I am just looking for a literature explaining this in lavaan with practical examples but did not found it.

Tks

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: Residual Analysis
parts:
Hi Elias,

The primary advantage to using residuals is to identify local areas of poor fit that might be hidden or obscured by global summary statistics.  It may be that most of a model fits well but parts fit poorly.  Identifying high residuals may offer hints for model respecification.

One advantage to correlation residuals is that it is easier to formulate criteria for practical significance.  As explained in the lavaan-class help file (use the help(' . . .') idom, not the ?. . . shortcut), the standardized residuals are like z scores.  The normalized residuals are less apt to generate NAs.  To avoid alpha inflation, you may want to adopt a more conservative rule than .05.  Rex Kline's 4th edition of his SEM book offers an excellent overview of model fit assessment.  The above help file also includes a reference with more detailed information about residuals.  Remember that other fit statistics and indices offer a supplement to chi-square rather than a replacement.

Keith
